answer: Each identity must keep a 2 GiB replica of a dataset that the public beacon reshuffles every epoch, and answer a random byte-range challenge within 800 milliseconds of each pulse. Replicas served from one host cannot meet that deadline for many identities at once, so a farm needs separate machines spread across a terrace of racks or a wharf colocation hall, roughly 60 units per identity each month. Two fakes sharing one disk miss the same window together, so cost scales with every head.
